passages.title: The Spring Clean-up
passages.text:
Last Saturday our street held its first spring clean-up, and I almost did not go. I had planned to stay in bed with a book, but my neighbour Ana knocked at eight o'clock with two pairs of gloves and a bright orange bag.

About thirty people met in the small square behind the library. A retired teacher, Mr Doyle, gave each group a map and a list of streets. Our group of six was sent to the river path, where rubbish collects after the winter floods. I expected the work to be dull, but the morning passed quickly. We pulled bottles, old shoes and even a broken chair out of the water. A boy of about ten found a bicycle wheel and shouted as if he had won a prize.

By noon we had filled twelve bags. The bakery on the corner brought bread and hot tea, and we sat on the grass talking to people we had passed in the street for years without ever speaking.

Nothing dramatic happened, and nobody thanked us in public. Yet when I walked past the river the next morning and saw the clean water moving between the stones, I understood why Ana had knocked on my door.

passages.title: A New Start at Forty
passages.text:
For eleven years I worked in the same office, checking invoices for a company that sold office furniture. The work was steady, the pay was reasonable, and I could do it with my eyes half closed. That was exactly the problem.

When the company announced that our department would move to another city, my colleagues were worried. I was surprised to find that I felt almost relieved. I had been thinking about a change for two years, but I had never said it aloud, because it sounded ungrateful.

I spent three months learning to use design software at a local college, two evenings a week. The first class was awful. Everyone else seemed to understand the instructions at once, and I went home convinced that forty was too late to start again. My teacher, however, told me to stop comparing myself with people who had been doing it for years.

In June I applied for a job at a small studio that designs signs for shops. I did not get it. In July I applied again, after they advertised a second post, and this time they said yes. The pay is lower and the office is noisy. I still arrive early every morning, but now I arrive because I want to.

passages.title: Two Days in a Quiet Town
passages.text:
My friend Ruth and I chose the town of Marlow for a weekend because the guidebook called it 'peaceful'. It did not mention the bus, which came twice a day and stopped running at six.

We arrived on Friday evening with two small bags and a list of places to see. The first thing we discovered was that the museum closed at four, and the second was that the only restaurant open was a pizza place beside the station. We ate there twice in two days, and I am not sorry.

On Saturday morning we walked along the river to an old stone bridge. A man was fishing, and he told us, without being asked, about the winter the river froze and the year the bridge was repaired. He talked for half an hour. Ruth kept looking at her watch, but I did not want him to stop.

The town had no cinema, no shopping centre and almost no traffic. By Sunday afternoon we had read our books twice and knew the name of the woman who ran the bakery. On the bus home, Ruth said she had been bored for two whole days. I said I had not been bored for a single minute, and we both laughed, because we were both right.

questions.prompt: The company decided to {{blank}} the meeting until next week.

explanation.zh: postpone 是「推迟」，until next week 说明只是改期，不是取消。
explanation.en: Postpone means to move to a later time; until next week shows it is not cancelled.

questions.prompt: He was {{blank}} for the mistake, although it was not his fault.

explanation.zh: although it was not his fault 说明他受到了责怪，blame for 是「因……被责怪」。
explanation.en: The contrast with not his fault shows he was blamed.

questions.prompt: She {{blank}} her teacher's advice and applied for the job, just as he had suggested.

explanation.zh: follow someone's advice 是「听从建议」；她后来申请了工作，说明听了。
explanation.en: Follow advice is the fixed collocation, and applying shows she took it.

questions.prompt: The weather was terrible, but we still {{blank}} the trip: the rain stopped just as we arrived.

explanation.zh: but still 表示转折：天气差，但旅程仍然玩得开心。
explanation.en: But still marks a contrast: bad weather, yet the trip was enjoyed.

questions.prompt: It is {{blank}} to eat so much sugar; doctors advise against it.

explanation.zh: 吃太多糖不健康，unhealthy 是「不健康的」。
explanation.en: Too much sugar is unhealthy.

questions.prompt: He {{blank}} his leg while playing football.

explanation.zh: 讲过去发生的事用一般过去时 broke；break a leg 是「摔断腿」。
explanation.en: A past event takes the simple past broke; break a leg is the collocation.

questions.prompt: The instructions were so {{blank}} that nobody understood them.

explanation.zh: 没人看懂，说明说明书写得令人困惑：confusing 形容事物。
explanation.en: Nobody understood them, so the instructions were confusing.

questions.prompt: We ran out of milk, so I {{blank}} some on my way home.

explanation.zh: pick up 在这里是「顺路买」；take off 是起飞/脱下。
explanation.en: Pick up here means to buy on the way; take off means to remove or depart.

questions.prompt: She is {{blank}} of spiders and runs away whenever she sees one.

explanation.zh: be afraid of 是「害怕」；interested in、aware of、tired of 搭配不同。
explanation.en: Afraid of means frightened by; the other adjectives take different prepositions.

questions.prompt: By the time we arrived, the film {{blank}} .

explanation.zh: 电影在我们到达之前已经开始，过去的过去用过去完成时。
explanation.en: The film started before we arrived, so the past perfect is used.

questions.prompt: He suggested {{blank}} a taxi.

explanation.zh: suggest 后接动名词：suggest doing。
explanation.en: Suggest is followed by the -ing form.

questions.prompt: I am looking forward to {{blank}} you.

explanation.zh: look forward to 的 to 是介词，后面用动名词。
explanation.en: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.

questions.prompt: She asked me where I {{blank}} from.

explanation.zh: 主句是过去时 asked，间接引语里动词相应退到过去时 came。
explanation.en: After the past reporting verb asked, the reported verb shifts back to came.

questions.prompt: The letter {{blank}} yesterday.

explanation.zh: 信是被寄出的，且时间是昨天，用一般过去时的被动语态。
explanation.en: The letter receives the action, and the time is past, so use the past passive.

questions.prompt: You {{blank}} smoke here; it is a hospital.

explanation.zh: 医院禁止吸烟，must not 表示「不许」；do not have to 是「不必」。
explanation.en: Smoking is forbidden here: must not. Do not have to means it is not necessary.

questions.prompt: If I {{blank}} more time, I would travel.

explanation.zh: 与现在事实相反的虚拟条件句：if + 过去时，主句 would + 动词原形。
explanation.en: A second conditional uses if + past simple with would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Neither Tom {{blank}} his friends were there.

explanation.zh: neither ... nor ... 是「既不……也不……」的固定搭配。
explanation.en: The fixed pair is neither ... nor ...

questions.prompt: It is the best film I {{blank}} ever seen.

explanation.zh: 最高级后接现在完成时，主语是 I，用 have。
explanation.en: After a superlative, the present perfect follows; the subject I takes have.

questions.prompt: He denied {{blank}} the window.

explanation.zh: deny 后接动名词：deny doing something。
explanation.en: Deny takes the -ing form.

questions.prompt: The more you practise, {{blank}} you become.

explanation.zh: the + 比较级, the + 比较级 表示「越……越……」。
explanation.en: The comparative ... the comparative ... means the more ..., the more ...

questions.prompt: When the shoes fell apart after a week, the shop agreed to {{blank}} my money in full.

explanation.zh: refund 是商店把钱退还给顾客，in full 说明是全额退款。
explanation.en: To refund is to give money back to a customer, and in full means the whole amount.

questions.prompt: It took us two hours to {{blank}} the top of the hill in the heat.

explanation.zh: reach 是及物动词，后面直接接地点；arrive 要加 at。
explanation.en: Reach takes a place as its object, while arrive would need the preposition at.

questions.prompt: She decided to {{blank}} the job at the bank and sent her CV that afternoon.

explanation.zh: apply for a job 是固定搭配，寄简历说明她是在申请这份工作。
explanation.en: Apply for a job is the fixed phrase, and sending a CV confirms she was applying.

questions.prompt: Mr Lee is {{blank}} the new project, so any questions about it should go to him.

explanation.zh: in charge of 表示「负责」，所以有问题要找他。
explanation.en: In charge of means responsible for, which is why questions go to him.

questions.prompt: I am sorry — I took your coat {{blank}} because the two look exactly the same.

explanation.zh: by mistake 是「不小心拿错」；道歉和两件外套很像都排除了 on purpose。
explanation.en: By mistake means by accident, and the apology rules out on purpose.

questions.prompt: There {{blank}} be a small cinema here, but it closed years ago.

explanation.zh: there used to be 表示「过去曾有」，从句说明现在已不存在。
explanation.en: There used to be describes something that existed in the past but no longer does.

questions.prompt: The last train leaves at eleven, so you had better {{blank}} it.

explanation.zh: had better 后接动词原形，否定式是 had better not do。
explanation.en: Had better takes a bare infinitive, and its negative form is had better not do.

questions.prompt: I would rather you {{blank}} anyone about the plan until Friday.

explanation.zh: would rather 后接从句时，谈现在或将来用过去式表示愿望。
explanation.en: After would rather, a clause about the present or future takes the past form.

questions.prompt: He left the office early {{blank}} catch the last bus home.

explanation.zh: in order to 后接动词原形表示目的；so that 和 in order that 后面要接完整从句。
explanation.en: In order to is followed by a bare infinitive, while so that and in order that need a full clause.

questions.prompt: You {{blank}} me you were coming — I would have cooked something special.

explanation.zh: should have + 过去分词 表示「本该做而没做」；后半句的虚拟语气说明对方并没有提前说。
explanation.en: Should have plus the past participle criticises something that was not done, which the conditional confirms.

questions.prompt: What did Ana bring when she knocked on the writer's door?
options: A map and a list of streets
Two pairs of gloves and an orange bag

explanation.zh: 文中说 Ana 带着两副手套和一个亮橙色袋子来敲门。
explanation.en: The passage says Ana arrived with two pairs of gloves and a bright orange bag.

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "dull" is closest in meaning to

explanation.zh: dull 指工作枯燥，与 boring 同义，后文的 but the morning passed quickly 也说明他原本以为会很无聊。
explanation.en: Dull here means boring, as the contrast with the morning passing quickly shows.

questions.prompt: What can we infer about the writer at the end of the passage?
options: The writer was glad to have joined the clean-up
The writer wished the morning had been longer
The writer was disappointed by the number of bags
The writer wanted to be thanked in public

explanation.zh: 结尾看到干净的河水后理解了邻居为什么来敲门，说明他并不后悔参加。
explanation.en: Understanding why Ana knocked shows the writer was pleased to have taken part.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to organise a group of thirty people
A boy who found a bicycle wheel in the river
A morning of cleaning that changed how the writer sees the neighbourhood
Why rivers are dirty after the winter

explanation.zh: 全文按时间写了一个上午的清理活动，重点落在作者对社区看法的改变。
explanation.en: The text follows one morning of cleaning and ends with the writer's changed view of the neighbourhood.

questions.prompt: What did the writer do two evenings a week for three months?
options: Checked invoices for a furniture company
Studied design software at a college
Taught a class at the local college

explanation.zh: 文中说作者每周两个晚上在当地学院学设计软件，一共三个月。
explanation.en: The writer spent three months learning design software at a local college, two evenings a week.

questions.prompt: In the passage, "relieved" describes a feeling of
options: gladness that a worry has ended

explanation.zh: relieved 指「松了一口气」，作者早就想换工作，所以部门搬走反而让他轻松。
explanation.en: Relieved means glad that something worrying is over, which fits the writer's wish to change.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about learning something new at forty?
options: It is easier than starting at twenty
It is a mistake unless the pay is higher
It is possible only if a teacher helps you
It is possible if you stop comparing yourself with experienced people

explanation.zh: 老师让他不要和已经做了多年的人比较，随后他找到了工作，可见关键在心态。
explanation.en: The teacher's advice about not comparing himself with experienced people leads to his success.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's attitude towards the new job?
options: Glad to have changed, although the job has some disadvantages
Sorry to have left the old company

explanation.zh: 作者承认工资更低、办公室吵闹，但说现在早到是因为自己想去。
explanation.en: The writer admits the lower pay and noisy office but now arrives early because he wants to.

questions.prompt: How often did the bus run?

explanation.zh: 文中说公交一天只有两班，六点以后就不开了。
explanation.en: The passage says the bus came twice a day and stopped running at six.

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "peaceful" means

explanation.zh: peaceful 指安静平和，下文说镇上没有电影院、购物中心，几乎没有车。
explanation.en: Peaceful means quiet and calm, which the town without traffic or a cinema confirms.

questions.prompt: Why did Ruth keep looking at her watch?
options: She was worried about missing the bus
She was waiting for her food to arrive
She had arranged to meet a friend
She wanted the fisherman to stop talking

explanation.zh: 钓鱼人讲了半小时，Ruth 不停看表，而作者却不想让他停下，可见她希望谈话结束。
explanation.en: The fisherman talked for half an hour while the writer wanted him to continue, so Ruth was hoping for it to end.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest at the end of the passage?
options: The same weekend can be boring for one person and enjoyable for another
The guidebook was completely wrong about the town
Small towns are better than cities for holidays

explanation.zh: 两人对同一趟旅行的感受完全不同，结尾说 because we were both right 正是这个意思。
explanation.en: The two friends felt differently about the same trip, and the closing line says both were right.
